source.title: Training, Reading, and Editing Legible Transformers

page_placements.theme: Feature pathways, circuit decomposition and compositional reuse

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how concepts are localized, redundantly represented, or distributed across units in trained transformers. Its results refine the superposition account: token-level features can be single-unit, while abstract concepts become distributed with depth. It does not reproduce the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses Toy Models of Superposition and cites results from other work; cited results are not recorded as rows. Rows below are limited to the paper’s own measurements of feature localization/distribution and related circuit structure. The tuned-lens vocabulary readout and editing results are not included because they do not measure the claim versions. The paper does not vary feature sparsity or importance, or test the original toy-model transition or geometry.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own 125M bounded-operator LM and measures whether conjunction computations live on single units or are spread across many. That bears on V4 (features spread across neurons in real LMs). It is a new, non-standard architecture, not the toy setup, so T3 fits better than T5. The paper does not argue against any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. More precisely, the authors say early-layer conjunctions are built redundantly (few operators, many copies) rather than distributed. Token-level features sit on single units. Abstract, nameless concepts are distributed across units, more so with depth. They call this the superposition of ordinary networks and claim conventional transformers plausibly share it, but measure a conventional model only in one attribution example. Decorrelation reshapes reuse rather than compacting concepts.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains a 125M-parameter transformer with bounded fuzzy-set feed-forward and attention operators, then measures representation structure; it does not implement the original toy-model method or test its sparsity/feature-count sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported distribution changes with layer and feature type; the decorrelation strength λd changes fan-in and fan-out. The paper also reports different results for early versus late layers.

fits_no_version.finding: A training-time decorrelation penalty shifts circuits from fan-out (mean ~21 readers per concept, hubs to ~1200) to fan-in (1.4 readers, ~15 input atoms), with no quality cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept reuse across downstream readers (fan-out) is a trainable circuit property, separable from per-unit feature localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct-logit attribution of 'than' spreads over ~1200 effective contributors in a conventional GELU model, vs ~31 (λd=0) and ~15 (decorrelated) in the bounded model. This is a single prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conventional transformers distribute per-prediction attribution across many components, more than bounded-operator models do.

record.problems: All numbers are single seed at this scale (125M parameters, one epoch). The feature-distribution evidence is mainly from a specially constructed legible model, with only a single illustrative conventional-model token-attribution comparison. The rank reconstruction is a causal reconstruction of the intersection block’s contribution, not a direct measurement of the geometric dimensionality of each feature. No feature-sparsity or feature-importance sweep is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Other measurements in the paper concern legibility training, vocabulary decoding, editing, or prediction explanations without directly testing the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy model, no sparsity sweep, no feature-count vs dimension manipulation, no geometry.
All of it: no capacity or feature-importance manipulation.
All of it: no test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
SAE or dictionary recovery of sparse features. Distribution in a conventional GELU LM beyond one attribution example. Other model scales and architectures.
All of it: the OMP decomposition is apparatus, not a test of SAE features.
All of it: no measure of whether a single feature is 1-D or multi-dimensional.

missing.what: Effective causal rank of the intersection block rises monotonically with depth, while the redundancy factor falls from 183× to 14×.
A clause/sentence-boundary operator is spread over 21 units with no single-unit reproducer, writes at vocabulary-ceiling entropy, and carries a small causal load.
A dominant activation mode explains 74–90% of block variance and is single-unit reproducible, but is causally inert at depth (rank-1 restores 3.7% at L10).

record.verdict_notes: Removed all V6 links: the rank of a block's reconstruction counts distinct operators, not the dimensionality of one feature. Moved the fan-in/fan-out and attribution rows to fits_no_version: they measure circuit reuse under an induced penalty, or attribution sparsity. Changed the tranche to T3: a novel bounded-operator architecture, not conventional neurons, so generalization to standard LLM superposition rests on the authors' assertion. All results are single seed at 125M parameters, one epoch.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, a sparsity-dependent transition, near-orthogonal overlap, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from causes other than capacity pressure.

Provides evidence about feature localization and distribution in a 125M-parameter transformer and a conventional comparator, but does not test SAE feature recovery or establish a general result across LLMs.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. Its sparse decomposition is described as apparatus, not a test of SAE features.
Measures causal reconstruction rank and unit-level reproduction of computations, not whether all superposed features are geometrically one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the layer-0 intersection block and added back a rank-r reconstruction of its residual contribution; rank sweep.
rows.measure: Share of the block’s ablation effect restored; operator redundancy and single-unit reproducibility
rows.value: Rank 4 restores 95% of the block’s effect; approximately 180 units per operator; a single unit reproduces an operator with activation correlation above 0.9.
rows.note: The authors characterize early-layer computation as a handful of operators replicated across the layer. This is evidence of localization/redundancy in this layer, not a test of toy-model superposition geometry.
rows.check: L0 conjunctions are a few operators copied about 180 times, each reproduced by one unit (corr >0.9). That is redundancy, not a distributed code. The V6 link is wrong: block reconstruction rank is not feature dimensionality.
